senses.gloss:
kaví, a. wise, possessed of insight (of gods,
esp. Agni); as m. wise man, seer, sage;
poet; pl. wise men of old^1 (whose spirits
hover about the sun), 91^12. [prop. ‘seer,’
√kū, ‘see,’ for *skū: cf. θυοσκόυς, *-σκοϝο-ς,
‘inspecting the sacrifice’; Lat. cav-ēre,
‘look out, be cautious’; Ger. schauen, AS.
sceāwian, ‘look,’ Eng. show, ‘cause to look
at.’]
[1] Correction submitted by Dr. Sampada Savardekar on 20210219. Reference: https://github.com/sanskrit-lexicon/csl-corrections/issues/52.

kaví-kratu, a. having the power or insight
(krátu) of a wise one; intelligent.
[1296.]

kāvyaśāstra-vinoda, m. entertainment
with poetry and science. [kāvya-śāstra,
1252.]
